label: q/o/f/d/0/a input in original phase (t>=2) of a sequence starting with t/k/y/s/j/r/2/3/p
explanation: Sparse unit (about 1% of steps). Most of its mass (68%) falls in the original phase, mainly t=2..4. It never fires at t=0 or t=1. It fires when the input is one of q, o, f, d, 0, a (each has 2.4-4.9x lift), and only when earlier context tokens come from a second set {t,k,y,s,j,r,2,3,p}, especially first_tok=t (7.7x, 39% of mass) and prev2_tok=t. The largest activations are sequences starting with t t followed by q/f/o/0 at t=3. The <DEL> step holds another 23% of mass under the same t-heavy prefix condition; adding it raises F1 slightly (0.35) but lowers mass recall, so it is left out. Copy-phase firing is weak (10% of mass). It is mostly silent on l, c, i, v, 1 inputs. The unit looks like a graded sum of prefix-token evidence and current-token evidence, so boolean predicates top out near F1 0.35; precision is the weak point.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the first original token (most: t, k, s, y, j, r; least: f, o, 0, d) and the current input token, by step (t=2: o, q, f, 0; t=3: o, q, f, d; t=4: q, o, f, d); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=1, L=4 & t=3, L=6 & t=5.
